summary: Intro discovery with Equinox Payments focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency needs, streaming and token/sec benchmarking. Equinox currently evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for card-reconciliation and fraud chat assistant. Main constraints: p95 & tail latency at 200-500 concurrent streams, SOC2/PCI concerns, and cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: share benchmark template, run trial cluster tests, provide Dedicated sizing + pricing, and share security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Gomez (Redwood CSM); Mark Rivers (Equinox CTO), Priya Nair (ML Eng), Carlos Mendes (Infra)

[00:00] Lina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Lina with Redwood, AE on the account, with Daniel our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:09] Mark: Hey Lina, doing good, thanks. We've been looking at your docs — quick heads up, our main focus is latency, p95, and throughput for our fraud chat and reconciliation flows. We also have PCI scope so security's a big decision vector.
[00:22] Lina: totally, understood. quick agenda — gather requirements (p95, concurrency, streaming), current infra, and then we'll map hosted vs Dedicated vs Private to your needs.
[00:32] Daniel: hi all, i'll jump in on the performance bits. can you share numbers you're targeting? p95, average, and expected concurrent sessions?
[00:40] Priya: sure, target p95 is 250-300ms for short responses (~50-80 tokens), and for longer synthesis 500ms p95 is OK. Concurrency: baseline 200 concurrent chat sessions during peak, spike to 500 for promos. Token/sec throughput matters because we stream. also latency tail is huge for user experience.
[01:03] Carlos: and we need predictable billing; hosted is easy but we worry about egress and data residency. we'd prefer Dedicated if it gives consistent p95, but need cost numbers. also private VPC/on-prem is a maybe for PCI.
[01:19] Lina: good. quick clarifying q — when you say 50-80 tokens, is that per response or per turn?
[01:25] Priya: per response, turns average 2-3 per session. sometimes longer 200-300 token summaries for batch recon jobs.
[01:34] Daniel: got it. our runtime has a bunch of levers — batching, KV cache/prefix cache, quantization variants. for short chat streaming we usually prioritize low-latency execution path with small batches and prefix caching to hit p95 targets.
[01:47] Mark: can you quantify — like tokens/sec or token latency numbers on e.g., a 13B model?
[01:55] Daniel: rough numbers, and i stress rough: on a high-end GPU instance with Redwood Dedicated we see sustained ~700-900 tokens/sec for a 13B quantized model, p95 generation latency per token under 10-12ms, but end-to-end response p95 depends on seq len and batching. for streaming short 50-token responses that maps to ~500-700ms end-to-end in some configs; but we optimize for lower — several customers hit 200-300ms p95 with tuned config and prefix caching.
[02:28] Priya: 200-300ms p95 is promising. is that for single-stream (1 user) or at concurrency?
[02:33] Daniel: that's observed at moderate concurrency (50-150) with continuous batching and cached prefixes; at 200-500 concurrency you have to scale Dedicated pod count or accept slightly higher p95 unless you use more aggressive striping and model sharding; we can route by policy to cheaper variants for background workloads.
[02:52] Carlos: what's the expected pod footprint for 500 concurrent streams? like how many gpus do we need?
[02:58] Daniel: depends on model size and throughput profile. ballpark: for quantized 13B serving ~700 tokens/sec per GPU — if each session averages 50 tokens at burst concurrency 500 and average think-time between tokens, you need roughly 3-6 GPUs to sustain. for worst-case long-run streaming (no think time) you'd need more; we can provide a dedicated sizing calc after you share session distribution.
[03:28] Mark: do you have a sizing template?
[03:31] Lina: yes we'll share our benchmark template — that'll collect sample prompts, session length distributions, and target p95. Daniel will then run a token/sec bench in our test cluster.

[03:44] Priya: a few more specifics — streaming: we rely on server-sent events and need steady token pushes within 50ms intervals ideally, else UI stutters; do you support chunked streaming and incremental partial tokens?
[03:57] Daniel: yes, we support streaming with chunked tokens and partial outputs. low-latency streaming at scale is where we tune batch windows tightly and prioritize low-latency inference paths. sometimes that means smaller micro-batches which increases cost.
[04:13] Priya: what's the tradeoff on cost?
[04:16] Daniel: micro-batching reduces p95 but increases GPU utilization inefficiency — so cost per token goes up. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching configs per workload. also Dedicated allows commitment to reduce unit cost.

[04:29] Mark: about hosted vs Dedicated — two things: 1) can hosted meet our p95 at peak? 2) will Dedicated give predictable SLAs?
[04:38] Lina: hosted can meet aggressive latency for many customers, but Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput and ability to pin model variants; for strict PCI/VPC needs Private is the route. Hosted plus burst capacity is often an easy first step.
[04:55] Carlos: security: we need SOC2 + PCI notes, KMS integration and audit logs. can you run in our VPC?
[05:03] Aisha: yes, we have Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integrations; we'll share the deployment checklist and SOC2 artifacts.

[05:16] Unattributed - Speaker 1: (mumbled) how do you handle KV cache eviction for long sessions? sometimes our sessions re-use context across turns.
[05:24] Daniel: we have KV cache management that supports prefix caching and selective eviction. for conversational flows we cache prefixes per session to avoid re-encoding system prompts. eviction policies can be tuned; for long sessions we hit memory limits and then spill to disk or recompute depending on profile.

[05:39] Priya: latency tail — how do you measure p95? is it generation time or end-to-end including network?
[05:45] Daniel: we report both: server-side p95 (inference) and end-to-end p95 (including network/HTTP/SDK). infra/SRE customers typically look at server-side p95 to size, and then add network overhead per region. we'll provide token-level traces in the Console.

[06:01] Mark: can you do a live benchmark for us? sample set: 50-token chat, 200-token summary, 300-token batch job. we'd like to see p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec at concurrency 200 and 500.
[06:12] Lina: yes. next step is to provision trial cluster — we can do hosted trial or spin up Dedicated nodes for a short pilot. which do you prefer?
[06:21] Carlos: we'd like to test hosted first to validate numbers, then move to Dedicated for stability. but for PCI we might need VPC later.
[06:28] Daniel: hosted trial's quickest; we'll run your prompt set and provide a benchmark report with p50/p95/p99 and token/sec. if you request Dedicated pilot, we can size it and run identical tests.

[06:40] Priya: a bit concerned about vendor lock and model variants — if we pick Redwood Dedicated and later want a different open model, will that break stuff?
[06:48] Lina: portability is a design goal — same API across hosted/dedicated/private. you can pin model versions or change them, and routing policies can fallback to compatible variants. there are performance differences by model family; we'll show recommended quantization profiles.

[07:02] Mark: what's the SLA for Dedicated? uptime and latency?
[07:06] Aisha: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for enterprise tiers; exact numbers depend on contract. we'll share SLA summary doc.

[07:15] Priya: about quantization — do you support 4-bit int8 variants? we've seen some quality regressions.
[07:22] Daniel: we support multiple quantization paths (4-bit, 8-bit, mixed) and we benchmark quality vs latency tradeoffs. sometimes 4-bit is fine for chats, but for summarization you might prefer 8-bit. Redwood Optimize recommends profiles per workload.

[07:40] Carlos: for the sizing calc, what metrics do you need from us?
[07:44] Daniel: session concurrency distribution, average tokens per response, percent of streaming vs batch, model family (e.g., Llama 2, Mistral, etc), and any seq len extremes. you said you'll share sample prompt set.

[07:58] Mark: timeline: we want to pilot within 2 weeks and production in Q2 if numbers good. is that realistic?
[08:04] Lina: pilot in 2 weeks is doable — hosted trial especially. Dedicated pilot may take longer for provisioned GPUs but still possible within 2-3 weeks.

[08:12] Priya: any gotchas on region latency? our users are US-east mostly.
[08:16] Daniel: choose region near users; also KV cache warm-up can affect p95 early in a spike. we recommend sustained warm pools for peak windows or pre-warming.

[08:27] Mark: about cost — can you ballpark cost for Dedicated vs hosted for the 3 use cases?
[08:33] Lina: we can give estimates after we pick models and session distribution. Dedicated reduces unit costs with reservations; hosted is pay-as-you-go. we'll include sample cost per 1M tokens for configurations in the pricing sheet.

[08:47] Priya: questions from infra — can we run some tests that simulate concurrent streaming where each session sends message every 1-2 seconds?
[08:55] Carlos: yes, we need real-world bursts.
[08:57] Daniel: we can run controlled load tests with your simulator or ours. for streaming every 1-2s we'll model steady-state concurrency. worst-case continuous token streams are the hardest.

[09:12] Unattributed - Speaker 1: (background) do you have any customers in payments?
[09:16] Lina: yes, a few finserv customers on Dedicated and Private. we'll share redacted case studies.

[09:25] Priya: about instrumentation — what telemetry do you expose?
[09:29] Daniel: token-level latency, per-request traces, cost per request broken down by token and model, model-level dashboards, and error rates. Console allows alerting on regressions.

[09:42] Mark: if we hit a sudden spike to 1k concurrency for a flash event, what's the fallback?
[09:48] Lina: routing policies can fallback to cheaper model variants or degrade to longer p95 but keep the system online. we also have burst capacity options for Dedicated customers.

[10:00] Carlos: about monitoring — will logs (audit) include question content? we have PCI concerns about storing card data.
[10:07] Aisha: audit logs can be configured to mask PII; Private deployments give you full control over logs. hosted logs are encrypted and can be configured for retention limits. we'll share the security doc.

[10:20] Priya: ok, can you run two benchmarks: 1) 50-token chat at concurrency 200 and 500; 2) 300-token summary batch at concurrency 50; include p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
[10:33] Daniel: yes we'll run both; we prefer you to share exact prompt set.

[10:39] Mark: anything else on our side? Carlos will gather infra metrics and Priya will assemble prompt set.
[10:45] Carlos: noted. I'll pull session distro and peak times.

[11:00] Lina: quick recap — action items: we'll send benchmark template, SOC2/security docs, pricing, and schedule the trial. Daniel to run benches once prompt set is received.

[11:12] Priya: thanks. can you also include example Dedicated pod counts for 200/500 concurrency as a ballpark?
[11:18] Daniel: yes — ballpark numbers in follow-up.

[11:25] Mark: ok thanks all.

[11:28] Lina: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with next steps.

[44:30] Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and filler words; some technical terms transcribed as KV cache -> K V cache, and "Red wood" in auto notes. The transcript includes natural interruptions and cross talk.
